chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it, said,
Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: The moderation (leads to) prosperity, and the extravagance (leads to) ruination.

key_terms.الْقَصْدُ: Moderation, balance, or straightness in conduct and spending
key_terms.مَتْوَاةٌ: Ruination, destruction, or that which leads to loss
key_terms.مَثْرَاةٌ: Prosperity, growth, or that which leads to increase

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on moderation versus extravagance in wealth and conduct?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise maxim from Imam Ali (AS) to define the spiritual and material consequences of financial behavior. The term 'mathra'ah implies a place of abundance and growth, while 'matwah' suggests a place of decay or ruin, establishing moderation as a divine law for sustenance. This principle is foundational in Shia ethics, linking economic discipline directly to spiritual well-being and societal stability.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, raising it, said,
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The moderation (leads to) prosperity, and the extravagance (leads to) ruination’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following: “’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Moderation leads to increase, and extravagance leads to destruction.’”
